note: The handoff. Per consumed source file: its SHA-256, the keys it yielded, the target table and legacy_ref it produced, the route and publish status, its relations and its asset references. This is verify-parity.ts's AUTHORITY, which is what lets parity run again after content/ has been deleted — at that point the flat files are gone and this record is the only statement of which source file produced which row. It carries no timestamp on purpose: meta.json records its checksum, and a stamp that moved on every run would make that checksum meaningless.
